chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Is it sufficient for me to say in place of the tasbih during ruku' and sujud: 'La ilaha illallah, wal-hamdu lillah, wallahu akbar'?' He said, 'Yes, all of this is dhikr (remembrance) of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What can be recited in place of standard tasbih during ruku and sujud in Shia prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that substituting the standard tasbih phrases with the declaration of monotheism (Tahlil) and praise (Hamd) during ruku' and sujud is valid, emphasizing the broad semantic scope of 'dhikr' (remembrance). This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary dhikr variations, provided the core intent of glorifying Allah is maintained. It underscores the principle that specific formulaic rigidity is less critical than the spiritual presence of mind in acts of worship.
